review_depth: source e-print read (uniqueness definition, Cor K_{2,t}(e), Prop p:K33, Conj; arXiv:2201.01798) + survey e-print (arXiv:2406.05509: Thm t:main TAR-iso => same X-sets after relabelling; still lists the conjecture as open) + own SAT computation and partial proof
summary: By the published reduction (Bong-Carlson-Curtis-Haas-Hogben 2023, survey Thm t:main), uniqueness of PD-TAR(K_{s,t}) is equivalent to: K_{s,t} is the only graph without isolated vertices on A u B having exactly its power dominating sets. Encoded exactly as SAT (minimal PD sets via forcing chronologies; maximal non-PD sets via forts; E != E(K_{A,B})) and solved with cadical: UNSAT (uniqueness) for (s,t) in {(3,4),(3,5),(4,4),(4,5),(3,6),(4,6),(5,5),(3,7),(5,6),(3,8),(3,9),(4,7)}; new beyond the source are (3,6),(3,7),(3,8),(3,9),(4,6),(4,7),(5,5),(5,6). (3,3) is SAT only via relabelled K_{3,3} (all-pairs family is fully symmetric; source proves it). Controls (2,3),(2,4) SAT as the source predicts. Partial proof: blocker duality shows the minimal sets N[fort] are exactly B u {x,y} and A u {u,v}; if every minimal fort Psi_xy with N[Psi]=B u {x,y} is {x,y}, then H=K_{s,t} (proved).
coverage: scripts/pdsat.py, pdsat_ablate.py, pdcheck.py; logs/pdsat-*.log, logs/abl-*.log (ablation: every constraint group is needed). CNFs removed (regenerable).
remaining: Lemma needed: for s,t>=3, (s,t)!=(3,3), no minimal fort Psi with N[Psi]=B u {x,y} meets B (equivalently, no "poor" q in B with N_A(q) in {x,y} together with "poor" p in A with N_B(p) in {u,v}). With it the conjecture is proved; a literal Lean endpoint would also need the TAR-isomorphism reduction formalized.
title: Uniqueness conjecture for power domination reconfiguration graphs of complete bipartite graphs
